B02C001.summary: Maya, a Danava craftsman whom Arjuna has just saved from fire and flood, offers to repay him. Arjuna declines and redirects the offer to Krishna, who asks Maya to build a grand assembly hall for Yudhishthira. Maya is welcomed by Yudhishthira, lays out a large site and begins the work, setting up the palace that will house the Pandavas' court.

scenes.B02C001S01: Maya, rescued by Arjuna, offers to do something in return, and Arjuna sends the offer on to Krishna.
scenes.B02C001S02: Krishna asks Maya to build a grand hall for Yudhishthira, and Maya is honoured and begins construction on a large plot.

shots.B02C001S01H02: Opening invocation to Narayana, Nara and the goddess Saraswati.
shots.B02C001S01H03: Vaisampayana says Maya, in Vasudeva's presence, thanks Arjuna for saving him from fire and flood and offers his services.
shots.B02C001S01H04: Arjuna says everything is already done, wishes Maya well and tells him to go freely.
shots.B02C001S01H05: Maya insists he is a great craftsman among the Danavas and wants to do something for Arjuna.
shots.B02C001S02H01: Arjuna tells Maya that he cannot make him do anything, and asks him to do something for Krishna instead.
shots.B02C001S02H02: Krishna reflects, then asks Maya to build a grand assembly hall for Yudhishthira, with designs that mix divine, demonic and human styles.
shots.B02C001S02H03: Maya is delighted, is introduced to Yudhishthira, tells the story of the Danava Vrishaparva, and marks out a five-thousand-cubit plot after a foundation rite and gifts to Brahmins.

B02C002.summary: Krishna, after staying a while at Khandavaprastha, decides to visit his father in Dwaraka. He takes leave of the Pandavas, Kunti, Subhadra, Draupadi and Dhaumya, and rides out with the brothers and priests following on foot. Krishna reaches Dwaraka, where he is welcomed by his family and the Yadavas, while Yudhishthira returns to his own capital.

scenes.B02C002S01: Krishna's farewells at Khandavaprastha, his ride out with the Pandavas, and his arrival at Dwaraka, followed by Yudhishthira's return to his capital and Krishna's welcome at home.

shots.B02C002S01H01: Krishna leaves Khandavaprastha after bidding farewell to the Pandavas, his aunt Kunti, his sister Subhadra and Draupadi, then drives off in his golden chariot and sends the Pandavas back after half a yojana.
shots.B02C002S01H02: Yudhishthira reaches his capital and sends his relatives away, while Krishna is honoured at Dwaraka by his parents, Balarama and the Yadava princes and enters Rukmini's apartments.

B02C003.summary: Maya leaves Arjuna, promising to return with treasures he had earlier gathered in the north: a great club, the conch Devadatta and a store of gems. He recovers them at the lake Vindu near Mount Kailasa, a sacred site linked to Bhagiratha, Indra and Shiva. He then builds a magnificent palace with gold columns and a crystal-stepped tank, guarded by Rakshasas, and reports its completion to Yudhishthira within fourteen months.

scenes.B02C003S01: Maya sets out for the treasures, describes the sacred mountain site, recovers the club and conch, and builds the palace for the Pandavas, which he reports complete in fourteen months.

shots.B02C003S01H01: Maya leaves Arjuna, collects the treasures near Mount Kailasa, describes the holy sites there, builds the palace and its grounds, and reports it finished to Yudhishthira in fourteen months.

B02C004.summary: Yudhishthira formally enters the new hall after feeding ten thousand Brahmins and giving them cows, and the day is celebrated with music and entertainments. A long list of sages, Kshatriya kings and Vrishni princes take their seats there and wait on him, and Gandharvas and Kinnaras sing for the assembly. The chapter sets the scene for the court that gathers in the new hall.

scenes.B02C004S01: Yudhishthira enters the new hall after feeding Brahmins and giving gifts, and the sages, kings, princes and celestial musicians gather to attend him.

shots.B02C004S01H01: Yudhishthira feeds and rewards the Brahmins, enters the hall to music and entertainments, and a long list of sages, kings, Yadava princes and Gandharvas take their places and attend him.

B02C005.summary: The sage Narada arrives at the assembly of the Pandavas, is honoured with a seat and gifts, and blesses Yudhishthira. He then questions the king at length about how he governs: his wealth, officials, spies, army, finances, agriculture, justice and personal discipline. Yudhishthira promises to follow this counsel, and Narada says such a ruler gains the whole earth and goes to heaven. The chapter presents Narada's counsel as the model of good kingship.

scenes.B02C005S01: Narada arrives at the assembly, is welcomed by the Pandavas, and begins his long list of questions to Yudhishthira about kingship and the fruits of learning, wealth and marriage.
scenes.B02C005S02: Narada asks about trade, artisans, the army's skills, public welfare and the care of the needy, and Yudhishthira vows to follow his advice.

shots.B02C005S01H01: Heading naming the Lokapala Sabhakhayana Parva.
shots.B02C005S01H02: Narada arrives at the assembly of the Pandavas, is described as a learned sage, is welcomed with a seat and gifts, and blesses Yudhishthira.
shots.B02C005S01H03: Narada questions Yudhishthira closely on how he rules: his spending, justice, officials, spies, army pay, farming, taxes, punishments and freedom from the kings' common vices.
shots.B02C005S01H04: Yudhishthira asks Narada how learning, wealth, a wife and knowledge of the sacred texts bear fruit.
shots.B02C005S01H05: Narada says these bear fruit through sacrifice, through use and charity, through a wife's usefulness and children, and through humility and good conduct.
shots.B02C005S02H01: Narada asks whether officials collect only fair dues from distant traders and whether merchants can trade safely in the king's lands.
shots.B02C005S02H02: Narada asks whether the king heeds wise counsel, pays artisans on time, guards against fire, snakes, disease and demons, cares for the disabled and homeless, and has cast off six faults.
shots.B02C005S02H03: Yudhishthira bows to Narada and vows to follow his advice, and gains the whole earth in time. Narada says such a king is protected and reaches heaven.

B02C006.summary: After Yudhishthira answers Narada's questions, he asks whether Narada has ever seen an assembly hall finer than his own. Narada says he has not seen one made of gems, but offers to describe the halls of the gods Yama, Varuna, Indra, Kuvera and Brahma. Yudhishthira asks for full details of each hall, which sets up the description of divine assemblies that follows.

scenes.B02C006S01: Yudhishthira replies briefly to Narada's counsel, asks whether he has seen a finer hall, and Narada offers to describe the halls of the gods, which Yudhishthira asks him to do.

shots.B02C006S01H01: Yudhishthira worships Narada and begins to answer his questions briefly.
shots.B02C006S01H02: Yudhishthira says he tries to follow the rules of duty and wants to walk the path of virtuous rulers before him.
shots.B02C006S01H03: Yudhishthira asks Narada, who travels freely among the worlds, whether he has ever seen a hall like his own or a better one.
shots.B02C006S01H04: Narada says he has never seen a hall of gems on earth, and offers to describe the halls of Yama, Varuna, Indra, Kuvera and Brahma.
shots.B02C006S01H05: Yudhishthira and his brothers ask Narada to describe each hall in detail, including its materials, size and attendants, and Narada agrees to do so.

B02C007.summary: Narada describes Indra's assembly hall, called Pushkaramalini, which Indra built as the reward of his own deeds. It is huge, bright and free of age and grief, and Indra sits there with his wife Sachi while gods, sages, musicians and celestial beings attend him. Narada says he has seen this hall and turns next to the hall of Yama.

scenes.B02C007S01: Narada describes Indra's assembly hall, its size and splendour, and the gods, sages, Gandharvas and Apsaras who attend Indra there.

shots.B02C007S01H01: Narada describes Indra's hall at length: its splendour and dimensions, Indra seated with Sachi, and the gods, Maruts, sages and celestial musicians who serve him.

B02C008.summary: Narada describes the assembly hall of Yama, the god of death, which Viswakarma built. The hall is free of grief, hunger, thirst and old age, and it is filled with dead royal and Brahmana sages who worship Yama. Narada says the crowd is too large to name in full, and he moves on to describe the hall of Varuna.

scenes.B02C008S01: Narada describes Yama's hall, a place of comfort, where many dead kings and sages, sannyasis, musicians and Yama's officers attend the god of justice.

shots.B02C008S01H01: Narada describes Yama's hall as a comfortable place of plenty, lists the many dead kings and sages who attend Yama there, and then announces the next description, Varuna's hall.

B02C009.summary: Narada describes Varuna's hall, which Viswakarma built beneath the waters and which has white walls and gem trees. Varuna sits there with his queen, served by the Adityas, serpents, Daityas, Danavas, personified rivers and seas, and mountains. Narada then moves on to describe the hall of Kuvera.

scenes.B02C009S01: Narada describes Varuna's hall in the waters, its gem trees and birds, and the snakes, demons, rivers, seas and mountains who worship Varuna there.

shots.B02C009S01H01: Narada describes Varuna's white hall within the waters, with Varuna and his queen, and the snakes, demons, rivers and seas who serve him, then announces the hall of Kuvera.

B02C010.summary: Narada describes the assembly hall of Vaisravana, that is Kuvera, which Kuvera built through his own asceticism. The hall seems to float in the sky, and Kuvera sits there with his thousand wives, served by Apsaras, Gandharvas, Yakshas and many others, along with the goddess Lakshmi and Kuvera's son. Narada notes that Shiva is a friend of Kuvera and often sits in the hall, and then announces a description of Brahma's hall.

scenes.B02C010S01: Narada describes Kuvera's hall, its beauty and its attendants, including Shiva and Parvati, and closes by announcing the description of Brahma's hall.

shots.B02C010S01H01: Narada describes Kuvera's hall in detail: its size, its floating gold chambers, Kuvera and his wives, the Apsaras, Gandharvas and Yakshas who attend him, and Shiva's friendship with Kuvera.
shots.B02C010S01H02: Narada's speech continues, describing the hall as attached to the sky and able to move through it.
shots.B02C010S01H03: The sentence ends, confirming that the hall is such as Narada has described.
shots.B02C010S01H04: Narada turns to the next assembly, the hall of Brahma the Grandsire.
shots.B02C010S01H05: A closing line of Narada's speech, introducing Brahma's hall.

B02C011.summary: Narada describes Brahma's assembly hall, which he was able to see only after the sun god Aditya guided him there following a thousand-year vow. The hall is beyond description, free of hunger and discomfort, and attended by sages, gods, planets, goddesses, ancestors and countless other beings. Narada ends his tour of the divine halls by declaring Yudhishthira's hall the finest in the world of men.

scenes.B02C011S01: Narada tells how he reached Brahma's hall with the sun god's help, describes the beings who attend Brahma there, and says Yudhishthira's hall is the finest on earth.

shots.B02C011S01H01: Narada tells how the sun god guided him to Brahma's hall after a thousand-year vow, describes the beings who attend Brahma there, and concludes that Yudhishthira's hall is unrivalled among human halls.

B02C012.summary: Yudhishthira asks why Narada named only one human king, Harishchandra, among the gods in Indra's hall, and what he did to earn that place. Narada explains that Harishchandra won heaven by holding the Rajasuya sacrifice with lavish gifts, and he passes on Pandu's message urging Yudhishthira to hold the same sacrifice, while warning of its dangers. Narada then departs, and Yudhishthira turns his mind to the Rajasuya.

scenes.B02C012S01: Yudhishthira asks about Harishchandra and Pandu, Narada recounts Harishchandra's Rajasuya and relays Pandu's request, and Narada leaves for Dwaravati while Yudhishthira begins to consider the sacrifice.

shots.B02C012S01H01: Yudhishthira notes which beings Narada placed in each hall and asks what deeds made Harishchandra worthy of Indra's hall and how Narada met his father Pandu.
shots.B02C012S01H02: Narada tells of Harishchandra, an emperor whose Rajasuya sacrifice was famous for generous gifts, and relays Pandu's message urging Yudhishthira to hold the same sacrifice, while warning of obstacles such as Brahma Rakshasas and war.
shots.B02C012S01H03: Narada departs, and Yudhishthira and his brothers begin to think about the Rajasuya.

B02C013.summary: Yudhishthira, stirred by Harishchandra's example, resolves to hold the Rajasuya but wants to be sure it serves his people. His ministers and priests urge him to proceed, and he weighs his own strength and resources. Because he wants a disinterested judge, he sends for Krishna, who arrives at Indraprastha, and Yudhishthira asks for his honest counsel.

scenes.B02C013S01: Yudhishthira describes his peaceful reign and reflects on the Rajasuya, his ministers urge him to proceed, and he sends for Krishna and asks for his counsel.

shots.B02C013S01H01: Yudhishthira broods over Narada's words, and the narrator describes his peaceful, prosperous rule under his brothers and why he is called Ajatasatru.
shots.B02C013S01H02: His ministers urge him to perform the Rajasuya, and he consults his brothers, priests and counsellors again.
shots.B02C013S01H03: Yudhishthira asks how his wish for the sacrifice can bear fruit through faith and speech alone.
shots.B02C013S01H04: The priests and sages say he is worthy, but Yudhishthira weighs his own means and sends for Krishna, who arrives at Indraprastha and is warmly received.
shots.B02C013S01H05: Yudhishthira explains the plan to Krishna and asks for honest counsel, since flatterers and self-interested advisers cannot be trusted.

B02C014.summary: Krishna explains why the Rajasuya cannot yet be held: Jarasandha of Magadha has made himself the dominant power over the kings, many of whom side with him or fear him. He recounts how Jarasandha drove the Yadavas out of Mathura, how the Yadavas founded a fortified city in the west, and how Jarasandha has imprisoned kings meaning to sacrifice them. Krishna concludes that the sacrifice cannot succeed unless Jarasandha is defeated and his captives freed, and he asks Yudhishthira to decide.

scenes.B02C014S01: Krishna surveys the kings who support Jarasandha, recounts the Yadavas' flight from Mathura and their new city, and says the Rajasuya requires Jarasandha's defeat.

shots.B02C014S01H02: Krishna calls Yudhishthira worthy of the sacrifice, lists the kings who serve Jarasandha, tells how the Yadavas fled from him and how he has imprisoned rival kings, and says the Rajasuya cannot proceed while Jarasandha lives.

B02C015.summary: Yudhishthira admits he is troubled by Jarasandha's power and doubts that the Rajasuya is worth the risk. Bhima answers that a weak king who starts a fight with a strong one perishes, but that Krishna's policy, his own strength and Arjuna's triumphs can bring Jarasandha down. Krishna argues that Jarasandha has already taken eighty-six kings and plans to make the number a hundred, so the fight must be taken up.

scenes.B02C015S01: Yudhishthira voices his doubts about Jarasandha, Bhima urges action, and Krishna argues that Jarasandha's captives must be freed and the sacrifice pursued through war.

shots.B02C015S01H01: Yudhishthira praises Krishna's wisdom, reflects on the difficulty of gaining imperial rule, and says he fears Jarasandha's power and whether the sacrifice is worth attempting.
shots.B02C015S01H02: Bhima answers that weak kings who provoke strong ones are destroyed, but that policy, strength and Arjuna's skill can defeat Jarasandha.
shots.B02C015S01H03: Krishna says the impatient seek reward without foresight, names earlier emperors who ruled by virtue, and argues that Jarasandha, though cruel, must be stopped before he takes his hundredth king.

B02C016.summary: Yudhishthira, fearing for Krishna, Bhima and Arjuna, asks that the plan to attack Jarasandha be dropped. Arjuna replies that courage and action, not fear, are what make a king worthy, and he insists that the Pandavas must fight. The chapter sets up the decision to challenge Jarasandha despite the king's reluctance.

scenes.B02C016S01: Yudhishthira says he is afraid for his brothers and Krishna and asks that the plan be given up, and Arjuna replies that valour requires them to fight.

shots.B02C016S01H01: Yudhishthira says he regards Bhima and Arjuna as his eyes and Krishna as his mind, fears Jarasandha's vast army, and asks that the plan be dropped.
shots.B02C016S01H02: Arjuna answers that valour outweighs birth and that they are capable, and insists that they should fight Jarasandha and win the imperial dignity.

B02C017.summary: Krishna argues that a warrior must fight, and that a secret attack on Jarasandha, who is too strong to face openly, is justified. Yudhishthira asks who Jarasandha is, and Krishna tells his origin: the childless King Vrihadratha of Magadha receives a mango from a sage, his two wives each bear half a child, and a Rakshasa woman named Jara joins the halves into one strong boy. The story explains how Jarasandha came to be so powerful.

scenes.B02C017S01: Krishna urges a secret attack on Jarasandha, Yudhishthira asks about him, and Krishna begins the story of Jarasandha's miraculous birth through the sage's mango and the Rakshasa woman Jara.

shots.B02C017S01H01: Krishna, called Vasudeva here, argues that a warrior must fight and that a secret attack on the too-powerful Jarasandha is justified, foreseeing his downfall.
shots.B02C017S01H02: Yudhishthira asks who Jarasandha is and why he survived close contact with Krishna without harm.
shots.B02C017S01H03: Krishna begins Jarasandha's story with King Vrihadratha of Magadha, who is powerful and rich but has no son, along with his two wives.
shots.B02C017S01H04: The sage Chanda-kausika gives the king a mango. The queens each bear a half-body, which the midwives discard, and the Rakshasa woman Jara joins them into one strong child.
shots.B02C017S01H05: The queens nurse the child and the delighted king asks the Rakshasa woman who she is.

B02C018.summary: Jara reveals herself as a Rakshasa woman who is also the household goddess Grihadevi, and says she gave the child to the king because she was pleased by the worship she received in his house. The king holds the rites of infancy for the boy and names him Jarasandha, meaning united by Jara, after which the boy grows strong.

scenes.B02C018S01: Jara explains that she is a household goddess who was pleased by worship and gave the child to the king, and the king names the boy Jarasandha and raises him.

shots.B02C018S01H01: Jara says she is a Rakshasa woman and household goddess whom families worship, and that she gave the joined child to the king because she was pleased with his devotion.
shots.B02C018S01H02: Jara vanishes, the king performs the infant rites and holds a festival, names the boy Jarasandha, and the boy grows strong like a fire fed with butter.

B02C019.summary: The sage Chanda-kausika returns and foretells that Jarasandha will become a mighty king whom no weapon can wound and who will see Shiva. King Vrihadratha then withdraws to the forest and dies, and Jarasandha conquers many kings. After Kansa's death, Jarasandha hurls a mace toward Mathura, and his allies Hansa and Dimvaka make him so strong that the Yadavas dare not fight him.

scenes.B02C019S01: The sage foretells Jarasandha's greatness, Vrihadratha retires and dies, and Jarasandha's power grows until the Yadavas hold back from fighting him.

shots.B02C019S01H01: The sage Chanda-kausika returns to Magadha, is welcomed by King Vrihadratha, and foretells Jarasandha's future power, invulnerability and vision of Shiva, after which Vrihadratha retires to the forest and Jarasandha takes the throne.
shots.B02C019S01H02: Vaisampayana says Vrihadratha dies in the forest, Jarasandha is granted boons and rules well, and after Kansa's death he hurls a mace toward Mathura, while his allies Hansa and Dimvaka make the Yadavas hesitate to fight.

B02C020.summary: Krishna says Hansa, Dimvaka and Kansa are dead, so the time has come to destroy Jarasandha, and he proposes a bare-armed duel in which Bhima will fight. He asks Yudhishthira to give Bhima and Arjuna as pledges, but Yudhishthira refuses and places his trust in Krishna's leadership. The three set out in disguise as Snataka Brahmanas and travel east toward Magadha.

scenes.B02C020S01: Krishna proposes a duel with Jarasandha, Yudhishthira sends the three off with his blessing, and they journey in disguise across many rivers and lands to the city of Magadha.

shots.B02C020S01H02: Krishna says Jarasandha's allies are dead and that he should be defeated in a bare-armed contest, with Bhima as the fighter, and asks Yudhishthira to pledge Bhima and Arjuna to him.
shots.B02C020S01H03: Yudhishthira refuses to give up his brothers, praises Krishna's leadership, and the three set out disguised as Brahmanas, crossing many rivers and reaching the city of Magadha.

B02C021.summary: Krishna points out the capital Girivraja and its protecting hills, and declares that Jarasandha will be humbled by being slain. Disguised as Snataka Brahmanas, Krishna, Bhima and Arjuna break a sacred peak and enter the city, where Jarasandha receives them with honour and questions their conduct. Krishna answers that Kshatriyas may enter an enemy's house by the wrong gate, and that they refuse worship offered in an enemy's house, so the challenge is set.

scenes.B02C021S01: Krishna shows Arjuna the city of Girivraja, the three break the Chaityaka peak and enter the city in disguise, and Jarasandha questions them and receives Krishna's explanation.

shots.B02C021S01H01: Krishna points out the fortified capital Girivraja, its hills and sacred sites, and says Jarasandha will be humbled by being slain.
shots.B02C021S01H02: The three break the sacred Chaityaka peak, enter the city in Brahmin disguise and take their seats before Jarasandha, who questions them.
shots.B02C021S01H03: Krishna explains that Snataka Brahmanas may wear flowers, that Kshatriyas act through strength, and that they enter an enemy's house by the wrong gate and refuse worship there.

B02C022.summary: Jarasandha denies that he has ever wronged the three visitors, but Krishna accuses him of holding many kings captive to be sacrificed to Rudra. Krishna reveals that he is Hrishikesha, called Sauri, and that the other two are the sons of Pandu, and challenges Jarasandha to free the kings or die in battle. Jarasandha accepts the challenge, installs his son Sahadeva on the throne, and prepares to fight, while Krishna decides that Bhima is destined to be the one to slay him.

scenes.B02C022S01: Jarasandha protests his innocence, Krishna accuses him and reveals their identity, Jarasandha accepts the challenge, and the duel is set with Bhima as the fighter.

shots.B02C022S01H01: Jarasandha protests that he has done no wrong to these Brahmanas and asks why they treat him as an enemy.
shots.B02C022S01H02: Krishna accuses Jarasandha of holding kings captive for sacrifice, reveals who he and the Pandavas are, and challenges him to free the kings or die.
shots.B02C022S01H03: Jarasandha replies that he takes kings only after defeating them, and accepts the challenge to fight.
shots.B02C022S01H04: Jarasandha installs his son Sahadeva as king, and Krishna, mindful of destiny, leaves the fight to Bhima, who is destined to slay him.

B02C023.summary: Krishna asks Jarasandha which of the three he will fight, and Jarasandha chooses Bhima. The two wrestle with bare arms for about two weeks while the crowds watch, and the sound of their blows is like thunder. When Jarasandha tires on the fourteenth night, Krishna urges Bhima to press the attack while his opponent is weak, and Bhima resolves to take his life.

scenes.B02C023S01: Bhima and Jarasandha wrestle with bare arms for about two weeks, and when Jarasandha tires, Krishna urges Bhima to strike and Bhima resolves to kill him.

shots.B02C023S01H01: Krishna asks Jarasandha which man he will fight, Jarasandha chooses Bhima, and the two wrestle with bare arms through many moves and holds, watched by the whole city, until Jarasandha tires and Krishna urges Bhima to finish him.

B02C024.summary: Bhima, urged on by Krishna, whirls Jarasandha in the air and breaks his body across his knee, killing him. Krishna frees the imprisoned kings, takes Jarasandha's celestial chariot, and the freed kings pledge to support Yudhishthira's Rajasuya. Krishna installs Jarasandha's son Sahadeva as king of Magadha, returns to Indraprastha, and then takes leave of the family and goes home to Dwarka.

scenes.B02C024S01: Bhima kills Jarasandha, Krishna frees the captive kings and takes Jarasandha's chariot, Sahadeva is installed, and Krishna leaves the Pandavas for Dwarka.

shots.B02C024S01H01: Bhima whirls Jarasandha in the air and breaks him over his knee, the people of Magadha are terrified, Krishna frees the captive kings and takes Jarasandha's chariot, and the freed kings promise to help Yudhishthira's sacrifice.
shots.B02C024S01H02: Sahadeva, Jarasandha's son, pays respect to Krishna and is installed as king of Magadha, then Krishna returns to Indraprastha with the Pandavas, takes leave of the family, and goes home to Dwarka.
shots.B02C024S01H03: The Pandavas' fame grows, and Yudhishthira rules his people while the brothers keep Draupadi happy.

B02C025.summary: Arjuna asks Yudhishthira for leave to conquer the quarters of the world and collect tribute, so the treasury can be filled, beginning with the northern region of the lord of wealth. Yudhishthira blesses him, and the four brothers set out to conquer the four directions. Bhagadatta, the king of Pragjyotisha, agrees to do whatever Arjuna asks, which opens the campaign.

scenes.B02C025S01: Arjuna asks leave to conquer the quarters for tribute, Yudhishthira blesses him and the brothers set out, and Bhagadatta pledges his help.

shots.B02C025S01H01: Heading naming the Digvijaya Parva, the conquest of the quarters.
shots.B02C025S01H02: Arjuna, having the bow, quivers, chariot and assembly hall, asks Yudhishthira's leave to conquer the northern quarter and fill the treasury with tribute.
shots.B02C025S01H03: Yudhishthira blesses Arjuna and urges him to set out with the Brahmanas' blessings.
shots.B02C025S01H04: Arjuna sets out north, Bhima goes east, Sahadeva south and Nakula west, while Yudhishthira stays in Khandavaprastha.
shots.B02C025S01H05: Bhagadatta agrees to do all that Arjuna asks and offers to do more.

B02C026.summary: Having won Bhagadatta's promise, Arjuna marches north and subdues mountain peoples and kings one after another, including Vrihanta of Uluka, Senavindu, Viswagaswa, the Kashmirs and the Trigartas. He wins many battles, collects horses and tribute, and fights a hard campaign against the Rishikas before reaching the White Mountains. The chapter shows the scale of the northern tribute that Arjuna gathers for Yudhishthira.

scenes.B02C026S01: Arjuna marches north from Pragjyotisha, defeats a series of kings and mountain peoples, collects tribute, and camps on the White Mountains.

shots.B02C026S01H01: Arjuna wins Bhagadatta's promise, then marches north, beats one king after another in mountain and frontier lands, takes horses and tribute, and camps on the White Mountains.

B02C028.summary: With Yudhishthira's consent, Bhima marches east with a large army and wins over the Panchalas, Gandakas, Videhas and Dasarnas. He gains the Dasarna king Sudharman as a commander, defeats Rochamana and the eastern peoples, and enters the lands of the Pulindas. He is then welcomed by Sisupala of Chedi, who offers his kingdom and entertains Bhima for thirty nights.

scenes.B02C028S01: Bhima's eastern campaign, his respect for the Dasarna king Sudharman, and his welcome by Sisupala of Chedi, who entertains him for thirty nights.

shots.B02C028S01H01: Bhima marches east with Yudhishthira's blessing, conquers and wins over many peoples, makes Sudharman his commander, is hosted by Sisupala for thirty nights, and then moves on.

B02C029.summary: Bhima continues his eastern and northern campaign, subduing kings from Kumara and Kosala to the foothills of the Himalayas, along with peoples of Kasi, Videha, Magadha and the coasts. He takes tribute of gems, gold, sandalwood, cloth and pearls, and receives large sums from the Mlechchha kings of the marshy coast. He then returns to Indraprastha and gives the whole treasure to Yudhishthira.

scenes.B02C029S01: Bhima's long campaign across the eastern and northern kingdoms, including Magadha, Karna and the coastal peoples, ending with his return to Indraprastha and his gift of the treasure to Yudhishthira.

shots.B02C029S01H01: Bhima conquers many kingdoms from Kumara to the coast, takes tribute from Jarasandha's son and the Mlechchha kings, and returns to Indraprastha to present the treasure to Yudhishthira.

B02C027.summary: Arjuna crosses the White Mountains and subdues the Limpurushas and the Guhakas, admiring sacred lakes on the way. At North Harivarsha, frontier guardians warn that the land cannot be conquered by a human, and Arjuna agrees to take tribute from them instead. He returns with horses, treasure and celestial goods and gives it all to Yudhishthira, who rests in his chambers.

scenes.B02C027S01: Arjuna subdues the Limpurushas and the Guhakas, is warned off North Harivarsha, takes tribute of celestial goods instead, and returns with the spoils for Yudhishthira.

shots.B02C027S01H01: Arjuna crosses the White Mountains, subdues the Limpurushas and the Guhakas, admires the sacred lakes, and at North Harivarsha accepts tribute after its guardians say the land cannot be conquered.
shots.B02C027S01H02: Arjuna returns to the capital with the horses, treasure and animals of the north, offers them all to Yudhishthira, and rests.

B02C030.summary: Sahadeva marches south and wins a long series of victories and tributes, from the Matsyas and Avantis to the Pandyas and the monkey kings near Kishkindha. At Mahishmati he is blocked by Agni, who backs King Nila because of a bond going back to Nila's daughter and an old boon; Sahadeva prays to the god, who relents and accepts him. Sahadeva then wins the southern and coastal peoples, receives the submission of Vibhishana, and returns to Yudhishthira with the tribute.

scenes.B02C030S01: Sahadeva's southern campaign, his battle with King Nila at Mahishmati, the story of Agni's bond with Nila's family, and Sahadeva's prayer to the fire god.
scenes.B02C030S02: Agni relents, Nila pays tribute, Sahadeva wins the Pandyas, Saurashtra, Rukmin and the coastal peoples, and sends messengers to Vibhishana, then returns home with the wealth.

shots.B02C030S01H01: Sahadeva marches south, conquers the Surasenas, Matsyas, Adhirajas, Avantis, Kosalas and others, and fights the monkey kings near Kishkindha before reaching Mahishmati, where King Nila's fire blocks his advance.
shots.B02C030S01H02: Janamejaya asks why Agni turned against Sahadeva, who was fighting for a sacrifice that honours the god.
shots.B02C030S01H03: Vaisampayana tells how Agni took the form of a Brahmana to court Nila's daughter, how Nila punished him, and how the god then granted Nila a boon and the city's women freedom.
shots.B02C030S01H04: Sahadeva prays to Agni, naming his many titles and asking for purity, strength and prosperity.
shots.B02C030S01H05: Vaisampayana says that whoever pours butter into the fire while reciting these mantras will gain prosperity and be cleansed of sin.
shots.B02C030S02H01: Sahadeva sits down to face the fire, and Agni relents, assures him that he was only testing him, and promises to grant his wish; Nila then pays tribute, and Sahadeva wins Tripura, Paurava, Saurashtra, Rukmin and the southern and coastal peoples, sending messengers to Vibhishana, who submits.
shots.B02C030S02H02: Sahadeva returns to Yudhishthira with the wealth and considers his campaign a success.

B02C031.summary: Nakula conquers the west, moving through the desert country, the Sivis, the Trigartas, the Malavas and many tribes and coastal peoples. He receives the submission of Vasudeva and the Yadavas and wins tribute from his uncle Salya, the king of the Madras. His treasure is so large that ten thousand camels can barely carry it, and he presents it all to Yudhishthira at Indraprastha.

scenes.B02C031S01: Nakula conquers the western lands, wins tribute from Vasudeva's Yadavas and his uncle Salya, and returns to Indraprastha with a huge treasure for Yudhishthira.

shots.B02C031S01H01: Nakula sets out west from Khandavaprastha, conquers the Rohitakas, desert lands, the Dasarnas, Trigartas, Malavas and many other peoples, receives Vasudeva's submission, and returns with a huge treasure presented to Yudhishthira.
shots.B02C031S01H02: Vaisampayana closes the account by saying that Nakula subdued the western lands that Krishna had once conquered.

B02C032.summary: Yudhishthira's rule has made his kingdom prosperous and his treasury full, and his advisers urge him to hold the Rajasuya sacrifice. Krishna arrives at Indraprastha with a great treasure, and Yudhishthira asks him to take part and share the merit. Krishna encourages him, and the Pandavas gather materials, priests and guests, and invite the kings and Brahmanas. Nakula is sent to Hastinapura to bring the elders, and the sacrifice begins.

scenes.B02C032S01: Yudhishthira's prosperous rule, Krishna's arrival with treasure, the request for his help with the sacrifice, and the gathering of materials.
scenes.B02C032S02: Priests are appointed, invitations go out, guests are lodged, the sacrifice begins, and Nakula is sent to bring the elders from Hastinapura.

shots.B02C032S01H02: Yudhishthira's just rule brings good rain, prosperity and a full treasury, his advisers urge the sacrifice, and Krishna arrives at Indraprastha with a vast treasure.
shots.B02C032S01H03: Yudhishthira thanks Krishna for his help and asks him to take part in the sacrifice, so that he may be cleansed of sin.
shots.B02C032S01H04: Krishna encourages Yudhishthira to hold the sacrifice, and Yudhishthira replies that his resolve is already rewarded by Krishna's presence.
shots.B02C032S01H05: Yudhishthira orders Sahadeva, Indrasena and the others to gather the materials and food the Brahmanas have specified.
shots.B02C032S02H01: The chief priests are chosen, with Dwaipayana as the principal priest, and workers erect halls and messengers invite Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaisyas and Sudras.
shots.B02C032S02H02: The guests arrive, the Brahmanas are installed and lodged, Yudhishthira is installed at the sacrifice, and the sacrifice begins with gifts of cows, beds, gold and maidens.
shots.B02C032S02H03: Nakula is sent to Hastinapura to bring Bhishma, Drona, Dhritarashtra, Vidura, Kripa and well-disposed cousins.

B02C033.summary: Nakula brings Bhishma and Dhritarashtra from Hastinapura, and a huge crowd of kings and kinsmen arrives for the Rajasuya, including the Kauravas, Salya, Jayadratha, Bhagadatta, Sisupala and Krishna's Vrishni relatives. Each guest is lodged in a white mansion and worshipped by Yudhishthira, who is seen surrounded by priests. The chapter ends with the closing formula of the section.

scenes.B02C033S01: Nakula invites the elders, the assembled kings and kinsmen arrive with gifts, they are lodged in fine mansions, and the section closes.

shots.B02C033S01H01: Nakula invites Bhishma and Dhritarashtra, who come with the preceptors, and a long list of kings and kinsmen arrive with jewels, including the Kauravas, Salya, Bhagadatta, Sisupala and the Vrishnis.
shots.B02C033S01H02: Yudhishthira assigns each guest a mansion with gardens, and the guests see him surrounded by priests, performing a sacrifice with large gifts.
shots.B02C033S01H03: The text notes that the section ends and gives its place in the Rajasuyika Parva of the Sabha Parva.
shots.B02C033S01H04: A short line completing the section heading in the Sabha Parva.

B02C034.summary: Yudhishthira asks the elders to help with the sacrifice and gives each of them a duty, from food and gifts to tribute and treasure. Krishna takes the humble task of washing the feet of the Brahmanas. Gifts and tribute pour in, and the Rajasuya is performed with six fires and generous feasting, so that gods, Brahmanas and people are all satisfied.

scenes.B02C034S01: Yudhishthira asks the elders for help and gives offices to each, Krishna washes the Brahmanas' feet, and the sacrifice is performed with lavish gifts and feasting.

shots.B02C034S01H01: Yudhishthira thanks Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Ashvatthama, Duryodhana and Vivingsati, asks for their help, and gives them the treasure to guide.
shots.B02C034S01H02: Yudhishthira assigns offices: Dussasana to food, Ashvatthama to the Brahmanas, Sanjaya to return honours, Bhishma and Drona to oversee, Kripa to treasure and gifts, Vidura as paymaster, Duryodhana to tribute, and Krishna to washing the Brahmanas' feet.
shots.B02C034S01H03: Kings bring tribute and jewels, the sacrifice goes on with six fires and generous gifts, and gods, Brahmanas and the people are all satisfied.

B02C035.summary: On the last day of the sacrifice, the sages and kings gather and debate freely. Narada recognises that Krishna, the Yadava, is Narayana in human form, and the elders agree that the first honour of the Arghya should go to the most worthy guest. Bhishma names Krishna, and Sahadeva presents the honour, but Sisupala cannot bear it and begins to rebuke Bhishma and Yudhishthira.

scenes.B02C035S01: The sages gather for the final day, Narada reflects on Krishna's divine nature, and Bhishma explains the rules for honouring guests and asks Yudhishthira to choose.
scenes.B02C035S02: Bhishma names Krishna as the first to receive the Arghya, Sahadeva presents it, and Sisupala protests.

shots.B02C035S01H01: Heading naming the Arghyaharana Parva, the taking of the first honour.
shots.B02C035S01H02: On the last day, the sacred sages and kings gather in the inner enclosure, speak freely, and debate with one another.
shots.B02C035S01H03: Narada, seeing the gathering, recalls that Narayana, the supreme god, has taken birth as a Yadava and is living among men.
shots.B02C035S01H04: Bhishma explains that six kinds of guest deserve the Arghya, and that the foremost of them should receive it first.
shots.B02C035S01H05: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to name the foremost guest.
shots.B02C035S02H01: Bhishma names Krishna, Sahadeva presents the Arghya, and Sisupala protests at the honour given to Krishna.

B02C036.summary: Sisupala denounces Yudhishthira and Bhishma for honouring Krishna, whom he calls no king and no priest. He lists worthier men who were passed over, including Drona, Duryodhana, Karna and Salya, and accuses Krishna of killing Jarasandha by treachery and of accepting the honour out of greed. He then leaves the assembly with the kings who followed him.

scenes.B02C036S01: Sisupala's long reproach of Yudhishthira, Bhishma and Krishna, and his departure from the assembly with the kings.

shots.B02C036S01H01: Sisupala rebukes the Pandavas and Bhishma for honouring Krishna, names many greater men who were passed over, accuses Krishna of unfairly killing Jarasandha, and calls the honour an insult to the kings.
shots.B02C036S01H02: Sisupala rises from his seat and walks out of the assembly with the kings who came with him.

B02C037.summary: Yudhishthira hurries after Sisupala and asks him to restrain his anger. He says the elder kings approve of the honour given to Krishna and that Bhishma knows Krishna better than Sisupala does. The chapter shows Yudhishthira trying to calm the quarrel before it spreads.

scenes.B02C037S01: Yudhishthira follows Sisupala out and pleads with him to accept the honour, since the older kings approve and Bhishma knows Krishna best.

shots.B02C037S01H01: Yudhishthira runs after Sisupala and pleads with him, calling his words improper and cruel, and saying the older kings accept the honour and that he should bear it patiently.

B02C038.summary: Bhishma replies that whoever will not honour Krishna deserves neither gentle words nor a compromise, and lists Krishna's virtues, deeds and place as the origin of the universe. Sahadeva issues a bold challenge to any king who objects, and Narada declares that those who do not worship Krishna are as good as dead. Sisupala, enraged, rallies the kings to block the sacrifice, and Krishna sees a great host of kings readying for an attack.

scenes.B02C038S01: Bhishma defends the honour to Krishna, Sahadeva challenges the objectors, Narada speaks, and Sisupala rallies the kings to stop the sacrifice.

shots.B02C038S01H01: Bhishma says that whoever rejects Krishna's honour deserves no courtesy, lists Krishna's victories and virtues, and calls him the origin of the universe, while dismissing Sisupala as a boy who does not understand.
shots.B02C038S01H03: Sahadeva challenges any king who cannot accept Krishna's honour to answer him, declaring his own foot placed on the heads of the proud.
shots.B02C038S01H04: No king answers, flowers fall on Sahadeva, a voice approves, and Narada declares those who refuse to worship Krishna as dead though moving.
shots.B02C038S01H05: Sisupala, red with anger, calls on the kings to battle against the Vrishnis and Pandavas, and the kings plot to stop the sacrifice while Krishna watches the gathering storm.

B02C039.summary: Yudhishthira, seeing the enraged kings, asks Bhishma how to keep the sacrifice from being wrecked. Bhishma answers that the kings are like dogs barking at a sleeping lion, that Krishna is that lion, and that Sisupala's folly is part of a divine plan to take back his energy. Sisupala responds to Bhishma with harsh words.

scenes.B02C039S01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma how to calm the kings, Bhishma compares them to dogs barking at a lion and blames Sisupala's folly, and Sisupala turns on Bhishma.

shots.B02C039S01H01: Heading naming the Sisupala-badha Parva, the slaying of Sisupala.
shots.B02C039S01H02: Yudhishthira, seeing the sea of angry kings, asks the grandsire Bhishma what he should do to protect the sacrifice and his subjects.
shots.B02C039S01H03: Bhishma replies that the kings are like dogs barking at a sleeping lion, that Sisupala is foolish, and that Krishna is the source of all beings, so Sisupala's folly is part of a divine plan.
shots.B02C039S01H04: Sisupala answers Bhishma in stern and rough words.

B02C040.summary: Sisupala mocks Bhishma as an old, misguided man and ridicules Krishna's childhood deeds, including the killing of Putana and the lifting of Govardhan. He accuses Bhishma of hollow celibacy and past wrongs, and tells the tale of an old swan who ate other birds' eggs until the birds killed him. He warns that Bhishma will die at the hands of his own kin.

scenes.B02C040S01: Sisupala mocks Bhishma and Krishna at length, accuses Bhishma of wrongs, and tells the parable of the old swan to warn him of his end.

shots.B02C040S01H01: Sisupala calls Bhishma a shameless old man who misleads the Kurus, mocks Krishna's childhood deeds, and accuses Bhishma of hypocrisy and past wrongs such as his treatment of Amba.
shots.B02C040S01H02: Sisupala tells the story of an old swan who preached virtue but ate the eggs of trusting birds until they killed him.
shots.B02C040S01H03: Sisupala says Bhishma is like the swan and warns that the kings may slay him as the birds slew the swan.

B02C041.summary: Sisupala praises Jarasandha for not fighting Krishna and accuses Krishna of unfairly slaying him, pointing out that Krishna entered in disguise and refused Jarasandha's hospitality. He calls Yudhishthira's advisers aged and womanish. Bhima, enraged, is restrained by Bhishma, and Sisupala laughs at him and calls for Bhima to be released so that the kings can watch him burn.

scenes.B02C041S01: Sisupala insults Krishna and the Pandavas over Jarasandha's death, Bhima rages and is held back by Bhishma, and Sisupala mocks him.

shots.B02C041S01H01: Sisupala says Jarasandha was worthy of respect, accuses Krishna of entering in disguise and refusing the host's hospitality, and mocks the Pandavas' advisers as womanish and old.
shots.B02C041S01H02: Bhima, furious, is nearly ready to attack, Bhishma holds him back, and Sisupala laughs and tells Bhishma to release him so the kings can see him scorched.

B02C042.summary: Bhishma tells how Sisupala was born with three eyes and four arms and how an invisible voice foretold that he would die at the hands of the one on whose lap the extra arms would fall. When Krishna took the child on his lap, the arms fell away and the third eye vanished, so Sisupala's mother asked Krishna for a boon, and he promised to pardon a hundred offences. Bhishma explains that Sisupala's boldness comes from this boon.

scenes.B02C042S01: Bhishma recounts Sisupala's birth, the prophecy, Krishna's test on his lap, and the promise of a pardon, and explains Sisupala's boldness.

shots.B02C042S01H01: Bhishma tells how Sisupala was born with three eyes and four arms, how a voice foretold his death, how Krishna's lap revealed his fate, and how Krishna promised to pardon his aunt's son for a hundred offences.
shots.B02C042S01H02: Bhishma says Sisupala now dares to challenge Bhima because of the boon Govinda granted him.

B02C043.summary: Bhishma says that Sisupala's defiance is Krishna's doing, since Sisupala is part of a divine purpose. Sisupala cannot bear the rebuke and retorts with a list of kings Bhishma should praise instead, from Karna and Drona to Duryodhana and Kripa, calling Bhishma as foolish as the bird Bhulinga. Bhishma replies that he holds the kings in no regard, and the kings threaten to kill him, while Bhishma invites them to fight Krishna.

scenes.B02C043S01: Bhishma says Sisupala's challenge is Krishna's will, Sisupala mocks Bhishma's praise of Krishna and lists other kings, Bhishma scorns the kings, and they threaten him.

shots.B02C043S01H01: Bhishma says Sisupala's challenge is not his own purpose but Krishna's, since Krishna is a portion of Hari who wants to take back his energy.
shots.B02C043S01H02: Vaisampayana says Sisupala cannot bear the rebuke and answers Bhishma in a rage.
shots.B02C043S01H03: Sisupala tells Bhishma to praise the other kings instead of Krishna, names Darada, Karna, Drona, Ashvatthama, Duryodhana, Jayadratha, Kripa and others, and calls Bhishma a foolish bird.
shots.B02C043S01H04: Bhishma says he regards the kings as worth no more than a straw, the angry kings threaten to kill or burn him, and Bhishma invites anyone wishing a quick death to fight Krishna.

B02C044.summary: Sisupala challenges Krishna and the Pandavas, and Krishna answers with a long list of Sisupala's old wrongs, from burning Dwaraka to abducting women. When Sisupala mocks him, Krishna throws his discus and beheads him, saying the hundred pardons his mother asked for are now used up. Yudhishthira holds the funeral and installs Sisupala's son in Chedi, the sacrifice is completed, and the kings depart while Krishna returns to Dwaraka, leaving Duryodhana and Sakuni in the hall.

scenes.B02C044S01: Sisupala challenges Krishna, Krishna lists Sisupala's wrongs, Krishna kills him with the discus, and Yudhishthira holds the funeral and completes the sacrifice.
scenes.B02C044S02: The kings take leave, the brothers escort them, Krishna departs for Dwaraka, and Duryodhana and Sakuni stay behind in the assembly hall.

shots.B02C044S01H01: Sisupala challenges Krishna and the Pandavas to a fight, calling Krishna a slave and no king, and Krishna answers the kings with a long list of Sisupala's wrongs.
shots.B02C044S01H02: Sisupala laughs at Krishna's claim about Rukmini and asks him to pardon him or not as he wishes.
shots.B02C044S01H03: Krishna calls up his discus, declares that the hundred pardons are used up, and beheads Sisupala, after which Sisupala's energy enters Krishna and the sky and earth shake.
shots.B02C044S01H04: Yudhishthira orders the funeral rites for Sisupala and installs his son as king of Chedi.
shots.B02C044S01H05: The sacrifice is completed under Krishna's protection, and the kings praise Yudhishthira and ask leave to return home.
shots.B02C044S02H01: Yudhishthira sends his brothers to see the kings to their borders, and the Pandava princes escort each of them according to rank.
shots.B02C044S02H02: Krishna takes leave of Yudhishthira, Pritha, Draupadi and Subhadra and drives off to Dwaravati, while Duryodhana and Sakuni stay on in the assembly hall.

B02C045.summary: After the Rajasuya ends, Vyasa visits Yudhishthira, who asks whether the omens have ended now that Sisupala is dead. Vyasa warns that the omens will bring destruction to the Kshatriyas within thirteen years, caused by Duryodhana's sins and carried out through Bhima and Arjuna, and he foretells a dream of Shiva. Yudhishthira resolves to bear hardship and to avoid harsh words and war for the next thirteen years.

scenes.B02C045S01: Vyasa visits after the sacrifice, warns of the omens and the coming ruin, and Yudhishthira vows patience and peace for thirteen years, while Duryodhana stays in the hall.

shots.B02C045S01H01: Heading naming the Dyuta Parva, the dice-play.
shots.B02C045S01H02: Vyasa comes to the completed sacrifice, is honoured by Yudhishthira, and Yudhishthira asks whether the omens have ended with Sisupala's death.
shots.B02C045S01H03: Vyasa says the omens will bring ruin on the Kshatriyas within thirteen years through Duryodhana's sins, and foretells a dream of Shiva, then departs for Kailasa.
shots.B02C045S01H04: Yudhishthira, troubled, vows to bear hardship for thirteen years without harsh words or war, and his brothers approve; Duryodhana and Sakuni remain in the assembly hall.

B02C046.summary: Duryodhana wanders the Pandavas' assembly hall and is repeatedly fooled by its crystal floors and doors, and the brothers and servants laugh at him. He leaves for Hastinapura in shame, and on the road Sakuni finds him sunk in envy of Yudhishthira's wealth and honour. Duryodhana declares that he cannot bear the Pandavas' prosperity and that Fate seems to be on their side, so he turns to Sakuni for help.

scenes.B02C046S01: Duryodhana is mocked in the hall, leaves in shame, and on the road confesses his envy of the Pandavas to Sakuni.

shots.B02C046S01H01: Duryodhana wanders the Pandavas' hall, mistakes crystal floors and doors for water and open passages, falls into a crystal pool, and is laughed at by Bhima, Arjuna and the twins until he leaves for Hastinapura.
shots.B02C046S01H02: On the way home Duryodhana broods on the Pandavas' prosperity and ignores Sakuni's questions, until Sakuni asks what is troubling him.
shots.B02C046S01H03: Duryodhana explains that he is consumed with jealousy at Yudhishthira's sway, his sacrifice and the tribute of kings.
shots.B02C046S01H04: Duryodhana says he would rather die than live with the Pandavas' prosperity, that Fate seems supreme, and asks Sakuni to tell Dhritarashtra of his grief.

B02C047.summary: Sakuni tells Duryodhana not to envy Yudhishthira, since the Pandavas' fortune has been earned, and lists Duryodhana's own allies, including Drona, Karna and Kripa. Duryodhana agrees to act with them, but Sakuni says the Pandavas cannot be beaten in battle. He then reveals a plan: Yudhishthira is too fond of dice to refuse a game, and Sakuni is a master of it, so they should win his kingdom at dice with Dhritarashtra's approval. Duryodhana asks Sakuni to put the plan to his father.

scenes.B02C047S01: Sakuni consoles Duryodhana, lists his allies, and proposes that Yudhishthira be challenged to dice, which Sakuni will win for him if Dhritarashtra agrees.
scenes.B02C047S02: Duryodhana asks Sakuni to lay the plan before Dhritarashtra himself.

shots.B02C047S01H01: Sakuni tells Duryodhana not to envy the Pandavas, since their fortune is their own, and that their gains, including Gandiva, Maya's hall and their allies, were earned.
shots.B02C047S01H02: Duryodhana says that with Sakuni and the great warriors he will subdue the Pandavas if the king approves.
shots.B02C047S01H03: Sakuni says the Pandavas cannot be beaten in battle, but that he knows how to defeat Yudhishthira himself.
shots.B02C047S01H04: Duryodhana asks Sakuni to name the way to defeat Yudhishthira without danger to his friends.
shots.B02C047S01H05: Sakuni says Yudhishthira loves dice without being skilled at it, cannot refuse a game, and that Sakuni is unmatched at dice, so Duryodhana should ask his father to permit the match.
shots.B02C047S02H01: Duryodhana asks Sakuni to present the plan to Dhritarashtra, saying he cannot do it himself.

B02C048.summary: Sakuni notices Duryodhana's misery and tells Dhritarashtra that his son is pale and despondent. Duryodhana confesses that the Pandavas' wealth and honour eat at him, and Sakuni proposes winning that wealth at dice, since Yudhishthira is fond of the game. Dhritarashtra agrees to consult Vidura, but Duryodhana threatens suicide, so Dhritarashtra orders a palace built for the match and sends for Yudhishthira, while Vidura, sensing disaster, warns against it in vain.

scenes.B02C048S01: Sakuni tells Dhritarashtra of Duryodhana's misery, Duryodhana lists the Pandavas' riches and his envy, and Sakuni offers to win them at dice.
scenes.B02C048S02: Dhritarashtra says he will consult Vidura, Duryodhana threatens to die if he refuses, Dhritarashtra orders the palace built and summons Yudhishthira, and Vidura objects but is overruled.

shots.B02C048S01H01: Sakuni, having learnt Duryodhana's mind on the road home, tells the blind king Dhritarashtra that his son is pale, emaciated and anxious, and asks him to find out the cause.
shots.B02C048S01H02: Dhritarashtra asks Duryodhana what troubles him, reminding him of his wealth, servants, food and pleasures.
shots.B02C048S01H03: Duryodhana replies that he is consumed by jealousy of Yudhishthira's wealth, lists the tribute of kings, the Brahmanas kept at the gate, and his humiliations in the crystal hall, and says he cannot find peace.
shots.B02C048S01H04: Sakuni says he is a master of dice, that Yudhishthira is fond of the game though unskilled, and promises to win the Pandavas' wealth for Duryodhana.
shots.B02C048S01H05: Duryodhana urges his father to let Sakuni play for the Pandavas' wealth.
shots.B02C048S02H01: Dhritarashtra says he will follow the counsel of Vidura, and asks that Vidura's judgment be sought before he decides.
shots.B02C048S02H02: Duryodhana says that if his father consults Vidura and forbids the match, he will kill himself, and that Vidura would then inherit the throne.
shots.B02C048S02H03: Dhritarashtra, moved by his son's threat, orders artisans to build a grand hall with a hundred doors and a thousand columns, and sends for Vidura, whose counsel he usually follows.
shots.B02C048S02H04: Vidura comes and warns his brother that the match should not be held, lest quarrels arise among the sons.
shots.B02C048S02H05: Dhritarashtra, accepting fate, tells Vidura to bring Yudhishthira to the match, and Vidura, grieved, goes to Bhishma.

B02C049.summary: Janamejaya asks how the fatal dice match came about and who supported or opposed it. The narrator begins to tell the story, and Dhritarashtra privately urges Duryodhana to drop the dice plan, praising Vidura's wise counsel. Duryodhana replies with a bitter list of grievances, including the tribute he had to receive, the mockery of his mistakes in the Pandavas' hall, and the laughter of Bhima and Draupadi.

scenes.B02C049S01: Janamejaya asks for the story of the dice match, the narrator agrees to tell it, Dhritarashtra urges Duryodhana to give up dice, and Duryodhana complains bitterly about the Pandavas.

shots.B02C049S01H01: Janamejaya asks how the dice match came about, who attended the assembly, and who approved or opposed it.
shots.B02C049S01H02: The narrator, a disciple of Vyasa, agrees to tell the whole story.
shots.B02C049S01H03: Vaisampayana says he will narrate the events again in detail for the king.
shots.B02C049S01H04: Dhritarashtra asks Duryodhana to drop the dice plan, praising Vidura's wisdom and listing Duryodhana's advantages.
shots.B02C049S01H05: Duryodhana answers that his prosperity brings him no pleasure, lists the tribute and the crystal-floor mockery, and says the laughter of Bhima and Draupadi is a wound.

B02C050.summary: Duryodhana describes in detail the tribute that many kings, peoples and tribes brought to Yudhishthira, from horses, camels and asses to gold, weapons and cloth. He says that many Brahmanas and tribes were left waiting at the gate, and that he lost his composure at such wealth. The catalogue shows the scale of Yudhishthira's power as seen through a rival's eyes.

scenes.B02C050S01: Duryodhana catalogues the tribute from kings, Brahmanas and distant peoples, many of whom were kept waiting outside the palace gate.

shots.B02C050S01H01: Duryodhana lists the tribute to Yudhishthira from Kamboja, the coastal lands, Bhagadatta, the one-legged and many-eyed peoples, the Valhikas, the Sakas and the eastern kings, and notes the Brahmanas and tribes kept waiting at the gate.

B02C051.summary: Duryodhana continues to lament by listing the tribute that peoples, kings and tribes brought to Yudhishthira, from gold and elephants to gems and horses, and says that many were kept waiting at the gate. He then describes the huge household that Yudhishthira feeds, including thousands of Brahmanas, and notes that only the Panchalas and the Yadavas pay him no tribute. The chapter adds to Duryodhana's resentment at the Pandavas' rising power.

scenes.B02C051S01: Duryodhana describes the tribute of many kings and peoples, and the vast household and feasts that Yudhishthira maintains.

shots.B02C051S01H01: Duryodhana catalogues the tribute from mountain tribes, Kiratas, eastern and western kingdoms, Virata, Yajnasena and Vasudeva, the gems from the Singhalas, and the kings who were kept at the gate.
shots.B02C051S01H02: Duryodhana describes the crowds of soldiers and servants fed in Yudhishthira's palace, the Brahmanas and ascetics who eat daily, and Draupadi who makes sure everyone is fed, and notes that only the Panchalas and the Andhakas and Vrishnis pay no tribute.

B02C052.summary: Duryodhana describes the coronation-style ceremonies of the Rajasuya, in which the kings served as attendants: one brought the umbrella, another the chariot parts, and Krishna bathed Yudhishthira with a great conch brought from the sea. Duryodhana says he was overwhelmed by such prosperity, which he says rivals that of Harishchandra. He concludes that he sees no point in living while his cousins grow in strength.

scenes.B02C052S01: Duryodhana describes the Rajasuya consecration in detail, the honours that the kings and Krishna gave Yudhishthira, and his own despair at the Pandavas' success.

shots.B02C052S01H01: Duryodhana describes the Rajasuya consecration, in which kings served Yudhishthira, Krishna bathed him with a great conch, and the Pandavas' conquests brought treasures from distant seas, leaving Duryodhana despairing that he sees no purpose in life.

B02C053.summary: Dhritarashtra rebukes Duryodhana for his envy, saying that Yudhishthira is free of deceit and that Duryodhana has as much wealth and as many friends. He advises Duryodhana to perform his own grand sacrifice, the Saptatantu, and to find contentment in his own rightful share. He warns that quarrelling with kinsmen brings sin and ruin.

scenes.B02C053S01: Dhritarashtra urges Duryodhana to give up his jealousy, reminds him that the Pandavas are his kin, and recommends his own sacrifice and contentment.

shots.B02C053S01H01: Dhritarashtra tells Duryodhana not to be jealous of Yudhishthira, who is honest and equally wealthy, urges him to hold his own sacrifice, and warns that quarrels with kin are sinful.

B02C054.summary: Duryodhana rejects his father's counsel and argues that a king must pursue his advantage by any means, since success is the measure of a Kshatriya. He cites precedent that enemies must be crushed while still weak, and says he will either take the Pandavas' prosperity or fall in battle. His refusal to be calmed sets the stage for the dice match.

scenes.B02C054S01: Duryodhana rejects his father's advice and argues for ruthless pursuit of advantage, insisting that he will seize the Pandavas' wealth or die trying.

shots.B02C054S01H01: Duryodhana tells his father that his counsel is confusing, that kings must act for their own advantage, that foes must be crushed while they are weak, and that he will take the Pandavas' prosperity or die in battle.

B02C055.summary: Sakuni offers to win Yudhishthira's wealth at dice, and Duryodhana presses his father to allow it. Dhritarashtra says he will consult Vidura and warns that hostility with the strong brings war, but Duryodhana argues that dice is a bloodless game that will raise his house to equal the Pandavas. Dhritarashtra gives way to fate and his son's wishes, orders a grand crystal-arched hall built, and sends Vidura to bring Yudhishthira to the match.

scenes.B02C055S01: Sakuni offers his dice skill, Duryodhana urges his father, and Dhritarashtra defers to Vidura but warns of war.
scenes.B02C055S02: Duryodhana argues for dice, Dhritarashtra reluctantly yields to fate, orders the crystal palace built, and sends Vidura to fetch Yudhishthira.

shots.B02C055S01H01: Sakuni boasts that he can win Yudhishthira's wealth at dice, comparing his betting to an archer's bow and arrows, and asks that Yudhishthira be summoned.
shots.B02C055S01H02: Duryodhana asks his father to allow Sakuni to play.
shots.B02C055S01H03: Dhritarashtra says he will consult his brother Vidura before deciding.
shots.B02C055S01H04: Duryodhana distrusts Vidura, who favours the Pandavas, and urges that his purpose be carried out at once.
shots.B02C055S01H05: Dhritarashtra warns that hostility with the strong brings war, and that Duryodhana is wrong to welcome such a thing.
shots.B02C055S02H01: Duryodhana argues that dice was invented long ago and involves no bloodshed, and asks that the hall be built so that he can gamble with the Pandavas as equals.
shots.B02C055S02H02: Dhritarashtra says he does not like Duryodhana's words, that he will regret them, and that the destruction of the Kshatriyas is fated.
shots.B02C055S02H03: Dhritarashtra, bowing to fate and his son, orders a grand crystal-arched hall with a thousand columns built, and asks Vidura to bring Yudhishthira for a friendly match at dice.

B02C056.summary: Vidura objects to his brother's order, warning that the match will split the sons of Dhritarashtra and destroy the family. Dhritarashtra replies that the world moves under fate, and sends Vidura to bring Yudhishthira. The chapter closes the first step toward the fatal match.

scenes.B02C056S01: Vidura warns that the match will bring dissension, and Dhritarashtra insists on fate and orders him to bring Yudhishthira.

shots.B02C056S01H01: Vidura warns his brother that the match will end in dissension and the ruin of their race, and says he cannot approve.
shots.B02C056S01H02: Dhritarashtra replies that the world moves under fate and tells Vidura to go to Yudhishthira and bring him to Hastinapura.

B02C057.summary: Vidura, sent by Dhritarashtra against his own judgment, goes to Indraprastha and delivers the invitation to a dice match at Hastinapura. Yudhishthira asks who the cheats are, and Vidura names Sakuni and other gamblers, but Yudhishthira says he will play only if summoned, since fate governs all. He sets out with his brothers and Draupadi, is greeted warmly by the Kauravas, and spends a night of revelry before the match.

scenes.B02C057S01: Vidura reaches Indraprastha and tells Yudhishthira of the invitation, and Yudhishthira asks who the gamblers are and says he will play only if summoned.
scenes.B02C057S02: Yudhishthira sets out for Hastinapura with his household, is greeted by the Kauravas, visits the family, and spends the night in pleasure before the match.

shots.B02C057S01H01: Vidura, reluctantly obeying Dhritarashtra, rides to the Pandavas' city and goes to Yudhishthira's palace, where Yudhishthira greets him and asks after the family.
shots.B02C057S01H02: Vidura says Dhritarashtra is well and invites the Pandavas to Hastinapura to see the new palace and to play a friendly match at dice, warning that cheats will be there.
shots.B02C057S01H03: Yudhishthira worries that a dice match may lead to quarrels and asks Vidura what he advises.
shots.B02C057S01H04: Vidura says he has opposed gambling but was sent by the king, and asks Yudhishthira to do what is right.
shots.B02C057S01H05: Yudhishthira asks who the dishonest gamblers are that will play against him.
shots.B02C057S02H01: Vidura names Sakuni, the king of Gandhara, and other skilled players, including Vivingati, Chitrasena, Satyavrata, Purumitra and Jaya.
shots.B02C057S02H02: Yudhishthira says fate rules everything, that he will not gamble at the king's command, and that he will play only if Sakuni challenges him in the hall.
shots.B02C057S02H03: Yudhishthira sets out with his brothers, Draupadi and the household, arrives at Hastinapura, is embraced by the elders and the Kaurava princes, sees Gandhari and Dhritarashtra, and spends a night of music and pleasure before the match.

B02C058.summary: The Pandavas enter the assembly hall, and Sakuni calls for the dice to be cast. Yudhishthira objects that deceitful gambling is sinful, but Sakuni argues that every contest aims at victory. Yudhishthira says he cannot refuse a summons, and Duryodhana offers jewels and wealth and names Sakuni as his player, which Yudhishthira objects to but accepts so the match can begin.

scenes.B02C058S01: Sakuni calls for the dice, Yudhishthira objects that deceitful gambling is sinful, and Sakuni answers that every contest is aimed at victory.
scenes.B02C058S02: Yudhishthira accepts that he cannot refuse, Duryodhana offers his stakes and names Sakuni to play for him, and Yudhishthira objects but agrees.

shots.B02C058S01H01: The Pandavas enter the hall, greet the kings and take their seats, and Sakuni calls for the dice to be cast now that the assembly is full.
shots.B02C058S01H02: Yudhishthira says gambling is sinful and not a Kshatriya's virtue, and asks Sakuni to beat him fairly rather than by trickery.
shots.B02C058S01H03: Sakuni says gambling is dangerous only in its stakes, and urges Yudhishthira to begin without delay.
shots.B02C058S01H04: Yudhishthira cites the sage Devala, saying deceitful play is sinful and that he wants no wealth gained by cunning.
shots.B02C058S01H05: Sakuni argues that every contest, whether of birth, learning or skill, is driven by a wish to win, and so dice is no worse.
shots.B02C058S02H01: Yudhishthira says he will not withdraw from a summons, that fate rules all, and asks who in the hall can match his stake.
shots.B02C058S02H02: Duryodhana offers to supply jewels and wealth and says that Sakuni, his uncle, will play for him.
shots.B02C058S02H03: Yudhishthira objects that gambling by proxy goes against the rules, but agrees to begin if Duryodhana insists.

B02C059.summary: The kings take their places in the hall, and the match begins. Yudhishthira stakes a precious pearl necklace from the churning of the ocean, and Duryodhana replies that he has great wealth to offer. Sakuni casts the dice and claims the first win.

scenes.B02C059S01: The kings take their seats, the match begins with Yudhishthira's pearls as the first stake, and Sakuni claims the first win.

shots.B02C059S01H01: The kings and elders take their seats in the hall, Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and Vidura sit behind, and the friendly match at dice begins.
shots.B02C059S01H02: Yudhishthira offers a precious pearl necklace from the ocean as his first stake and asks what Duryodhana will wager.
shots.B02C059S01H03: Duryodhana says he has much wealth, but asks Yudhishthira to take that stake.
shots.B02C059S01H04: Sakuni, skilled at dice, casts them and says that he has won.

B02C060.summary: Yudhishthira keeps staking his riches, from his gold and treasure to chariots, serving-girls, servants, elephants, horses, warriors and jewels, and Sakuni claims each stake in turn. Yudhishthira protests that the wins are unfair but keeps playing. The chapter shows the match growing into a steady loss for the Pandavas.

scenes.B02C060S01: Yudhishthira stakes his treasury, his royal chariot and a hundred thousand serving-girls, and Sakuni claims each.
scenes.B02C060S02: Yudhishthira stakes thousands of servants and a thousand elephants, and Sakuni claims them.
scenes.B02C060S03: Yudhishthira stakes chariots, warriors and the horses that Chitraratha gave Arjuna, and Sakuni claims them.
scenes.B02C060S04: Yudhishthira stakes ten thousand chariots, sixty thousand warriors and four hundred jewels, and Sakuni claims them all.

shots.B02C060S01H01: Yudhishthira says Sakuni has won unfairly and stakes his treasury of gold, silver and jars of coins.
shots.B02C060S01H03: Yudhishthira stakes his royal chariot, drawn by eight white steeds and decked with bells.
shots.B02C060S01H05: Yudhishthira stakes a hundred thousand young serving-girls, skilled in the arts and in attendance on kings and Brahmanas.
shots.B02C060S02H02: Yudhishthira stakes thousands of serving-men, trained to wait on guests.
shots.B02C060S02H04: Yudhishthira stakes a thousand elephants with golden girdles and their attendants.
shots.B02C060S02H05: Sakuni laughs and claims the elephants.
shots.B02C060S03H01: Yudhishthira stakes as many cars as elephants, with trained horses and warriors paid a monthly wage.
shots.B02C060S03H02: The narrator calls Sakuni a wretch pledged to enmity, and says he continues.
shots.B02C060S03H03: Sakuni claims the cars and warriors.
shots.B02C060S03H04: Yudhishthira stakes the horses that Chitraratha gave Arjuna.
shots.B02C060S04H01: Yudhishthira stakes ten thousand cars and sixty thousand picked warriors.
shots.B02C060S04H03: Yudhishthira stakes four hundred gem-filled caskets of gold.
shots.B02C060S04H04: Sakuni claims the four hundred caskets.

B02C061.summary: During the match Vidura warns Dhritarashtra that Duryodhana, who cried like a jackal from birth, will bring ruin on the family. He illustrates the danger with the tale of the honey-gatherers who fall from heights and the king who killed his golden birds, and urges Dhritarashtra to stop pursuing the Pandavas for gain. He warns that the Yadavas once rid themselves of a bad son for the good of the whole, and suggests that war with the Pandavas would be disastrous.

scenes.B02C061S01: Vidura warns Dhritarashtra in a long speech that Duryodhana is ruinous and that the match should be halted before it brings disaster.

shots.B02C061S01H01: Vidura warns Dhritarashtra that Duryodhana is a jackal in human form who will destroy the family, quotes Sukra and fables of honey-gatherers and golden birds, and urges him not to pursue the Pandavas for gain or to send his sons to Yama's realm.

B02C062.summary: Vidura continues his plea that gambling sows dissension and that Duryodhana's intoxication will drive away the family's luck. He warns the Kauravas not to enter the fire that Duryodhana has lit, and asks why Dhritarashtra wants the Pandavas' wealth when he could win the Pandavas themselves as allies. He calls on Sakuni to go home and urges the king to avoid war with the sons of Pandu.

scenes.B02C062S01: Vidura's second plea to Dhritarashtra and the Kauravas, urging them to stop the match, avoid war and send Sakuni home.

shots.B02C062S01H01: Vidura says gambling is the root of quarrels, that Duryodhana's intoxication will ruin the Kauravas, and urges the Kauravas not to enter the fire, asking why Dhritarashtra would take wealth rather than win the Pandavas as allies, and telling Sakuni to return home.

B02C063.summary: Duryodhana rounds on Vidura, accusing him of favouring the Pandavas, of speaking harsh words, and of being a parasite who should leave the king's service. Vidura answers that a king who casts off honest counsellors is like a child who quarrels with his friend, and that a man who turns on his wise advisers invites ruin. He then bows to Dhritarashtra and takes his leave, marking a sharp split in the court.

scenes.B02C063S01: Duryodhana rebukes Vidura for opposing him, Vidura replies that the wise must speak plainly, and then Vidura takes his leave.

shots.B02C063S01H01: Duryodhana accuses Vidura of favouring the Pandavas, of harsh words and of hostility under a show of loyalty, and tells him to go wherever he likes.
shots.B02C063S01H02: Vidura answers Dhritarashtra that kings who cast off honest counsellors are like fickle children, that Duryodhana is foolish, and that he takes his leave, wishing the family well.

B02C064.summary: Sakuni keeps pressing Yudhishthira for more stakes, and Yudhishthira stakes his wealth, lands and people, then his brothers one by one, then himself, and finally Draupadi. Sakuni wins each stake in turn. The elders cry out in horror, Vidura sits in grief, Dhritarashtra keeps asking whether the stake has been won, and Karna and Dussasana laugh.

scenes.B02C064S01: Sakuni asks for more, and Yudhishthira stakes his untold wealth, cattle and herds, which Sakuni wins.
scenes.B02C064S02: Yudhishthira stakes his city, lands, people and princes in their ornaments, and Nakula last, and Sakuni wins them.
scenes.B02C064S03: Sakuni points out that Nakula is already won, and Yudhishthira stakes Sahadeva, whom Sakuni also wins.
scenes.B02C064S04: Sakuni taunts Yudhishthira about the twins, Yudhishthira rebukes him, and Yudhishthira stakes Arjuna, whom Sakuni wins.
scenes.B02C064S05: Sakuni claims Arjuna and urges Yudhishthira to stake Bhima, then asks whether anything remains, and Yudhishthira stakes himself.
scenes.B02C064S06: Sakuni wins Yudhishthira, urges him to stake Draupadi to win himself back, and Yudhishthira does so while the assembly is horrified and Sakuni wins again.

shots.B02C064S01H01: Sakuni asks Yudhishthira whether he has any wealth left unstaked.
shots.B02C064S01H02: Yudhishthira says he has untold wealth and stakes it in huge numbers.
shots.B02C064S01H04: Yudhishthira stakes his herds of cattle, horses and sheep across the lands from the Parnasa to the Sindhu.
shots.B02C064S02H01: Yudhishthira stakes his city, the lands, the wealth and the people, except the Brahmanas.
shots.B02C064S02H03: Yudhishthira stakes the princes, adorned in jewels and earrings.
shots.B02C064S02H05: Yudhishthira stakes Nakula, strong and red-eyed.
shots.B02C064S03H01: Sakuni notes that Nakula is already in his power, and asks what stake Yudhishthira will offer next.
shots.B02C064S03H03: Sakuni declares that Nakula has been won.
shots.B02C064S03H04: Yudhishthira stakes Sahadeva, who administers justice and is learned.
shots.B02C064S04H01: Sakuni says the twins, dear to Yudhishthira, are already won, and asks whether Bhima and Arjuna are dearer still.
shots.B02C064S04H02: Yudhishthira calls Sakuni a wretch for sowing disunion among brothers who share one heart.
shots.B02C064S04H03: Sakuni offers an apology, saying that gamblers rave in play and do not recall it afterwards.
shots.B02C064S04H04: Yudhishthira stakes Arjuna, the great archer and leader.
shots.B02C064S05H01: Sakuni says Arjuna is now won and urges Yudhishthira to play with Bhima.
shots.B02C064S05H02: Yudhishthira stakes Bhima, the mace-wielder who is unmatched in strength.
shots.B02C064S05H04: Sakuni asks whether Yudhishthira still has anything that has not been lost.
shots.B02C064S05H05: Yudhishthira says that only he, the eldest, is still unwon, and that he will accept whatever the winner decides.
shots.B02C064S06H02: Sakuni tells Yudhishthira that staking himself is sinful, since wealth remains to him.
shots.B02C064S06H03: Sakuni urges Yudhishthira to stake Draupadi to win himself back.
shots.B02C064S06H04: Yudhishthira stakes Draupadi, praising her beauty and virtue.
shots.B02C064S06H05: The elders cry out in shame, Bhishma, Drona and Kripa sweat, Vidura sits in grief, Dhritarashtra keeps asking whether it has been won, and Karna and Dussasana laugh, while Sakuni takes up the dice and claims the win.

B02C065.summary: Duryodhana orders Vidura to bring Draupadi into the hall and make her a servant. Vidura warns him sharply that he is tying himself in cords and courting ruin, and argues that Draupadi cannot be enslaved, since Yudhishthira had already lost himself before staking her. He ends with the fable of the goat that swallowed a hook, urging Duryodhana not to swallow the Pandavas' wealth or make them enemies.

scenes.B02C065S01: Duryodhana orders Draupadi brought in as a slave, and Vidura warns him that he is courting ruin and that Draupadi cannot be lawfully staked.

shots.B02C065S01H01: Duryodhana orders Vidura to bring Draupadi to sweep the rooms and stay with the serving-women.
shots.B02C065S01H02: Vidura warns Duryodhana that he is courting ruin, argues that Draupadi cannot be enslaved since Yudhishthira had already lost himself, and tells the fable of the goat that swallowed a hook to urge him to stop.

B02C066.summary: Duryodhana sends a messenger to bring Draupadi into the assembly. She asks whether Yudhishthira staked himself or her first, and no one can answer, so Duryodhana has Dussasana drag her by the hair before the hall. She pleads that she is in her season and wearing one garment, and the elders stay silent while the Pandavas burn with anger. Vikarna argues that Draupadi was not validly won, Karna rebukes him, and Dussasana tries to strip her, but a miracle of endless robes saves her, and Vidura cites the tale of Prahlada to urge the assembly to answer. The chapter is the moral low point of the match and sets up the vows of vengeance that follow.

scenes.B02C066S01: Duryodhana sends the messenger to fetch Draupadi, and she asks whether Yudhishthira staked himself or her first.
scenes.B02C066S02: The messenger returns with Draupadi's question, Yudhishthira stays silent, and Duryodhana insists that Draupadi come to the hall.
scenes.B02C066S03: Dussasana drags Draupadi by her hair before the assembly, she pleads that she is in her season, and the elders fail to stop him.
scenes.B02C066S04: Bhima rages and offers to burn Yudhishthira's hands, Arjuna restrains him, and Vikarna argues that Draupadi was not validly won.
scenes.B02C066S05: Karna rebukes Vikarna, Dussasana tries to strip Draupadi, a miracle of endless robes protects her, Bhima swears to kill Dussasana, and Vidura cites the tale of Prahlada.
scenes.B02C066S06: Vidura asks the assembly to answer Draupadi's question, but Karna orders her dragged to the inner apartments.

shots.B02C066S01H01: Duryodhana, drunk with pride, orders the messenger to bring Draupadi, saying Vidura alone is afraid and the Pandavas have nothing to fear.
shots.B02C066S01H02: The messenger, a Suta, goes into the Pandavas' quarters and tells Draupadi that Duryodhana has won her and that she must come to the palace as a servant.
shots.B02C066S01H03: Draupadi asks how any prince could stake his wife, and says the king must have been mad with dice.
shots.B02C066S01H04: The messenger says Yudhishthira first staked his brothers, then himself, then Draupadi.
shots.B02C066S01H05: Draupadi asks the messenger to find out from the gambler whether he lost himself first or her.
