shots.B02C066S02H01: The messenger takes Draupadi's question to the assembly, and Yudhishthira sits silent like one out of his mind.
shots.B02C066S02H02: Duryodhana orders that Draupadi come into the hall to put her question before everyone.
shots.B02C066S02H03: The messenger returns to Draupadi, distressed, and warns her that the Kauravas' end is near.
shots.B02C066S02H04: Draupadi says morality should guide them and asks the elders to say what she must do.
shots.B02C066S02H05: The messenger brings her reply back, but the assembly sits silent with lowered faces.
shots.B02C066S03H01: Yudhishthira sends word that Draupadi should come weeping before her father-in-law, while Duryodhana orders the messenger to fetch her and the messenger hesitates in fear.
shots.B02C066S03H02: Duryodhana sends his brother Dussasana, who goes to Draupadi, calls her a slave, seizes her by her locks and drags her toward the hall.
shots.B02C066S03H03: Draupadi, dragged and half-clothed, cries out that the elders are silent, that virtue has vanished, and that Bhishma, Drona and Vidura have lost their energy.
shots.B02C066S03H04: Draupadi's look enrages the Pandavas, Dussasana calls her a slave, Karna and Sakuni applaud, and Bhishma says the question is too subtle to decide.
shots.B02C066S03H05: Draupadi answers that Yudhishthira was summoned and tricked by cheats and cannot have staked her willingly, and asks the Kurus to judge.
shots.B02C066S04H01: Dussasana insults Draupadi, and Bhima, seeing her in her distress, fixes his anger on Yudhishthira.
shots.B02C066S04H02: Bhima protests that Draupadi, the wife of the Pandavas, does not deserve this, and says he will burn Yudhishthira's hands, asking Sahadeva to bring fire.
shots.B02C066S04H03: Arjuna asks Bhima not to fulfil the enemy's wishes, saying Yudhishthira acted under Kshatriya usage after being summoned.
shots.B02C066S04H04: Bhima says that if he had not known Yudhishthira acted by Kshatriya custom, he would have burned his hands.
shots.B02C066S04H05: Vikarna, a son of Dhritarashtra, urges the kings to answer Draupadi, and then argues that the vices of kings make the staking void, so Draupadi was not won.
shots.B02C066S05H01: Karna rebukes Vikarna as a boy, says Draupadi was won fairly, and orders Dussasana to strip the Pandavas' upper garments and Draupadi's clothing, which he begins.
shots.B02C066S05H02: Draupadi calls on Krishna to save her, and Dharma covers her with robes that keep appearing as each is pulled off.
shots.B02C066S05H03: Bhima swears in the hearing of the kings that he will tear open Dussasana's breast and drink his blood.
shots.B02C066S05H04: The assembly cries shame on Dussasana, Vidura calls for an answer to Draupadi's question, and he argues that silence in the face of injustice shares its guilt.
shots.B02C066S05H05: Vidura tells the tale of Prahlada, who was asked to judge a wager between Virochana and Sudhanwan and was taught by Kasyapa that a lie before an assembly brings sin.
shots.B02C066S06H01: Vidura urges everyone present to think carefully about the answer Draupadi needs.
shots.B02C066S06H02: The kings say nothing, Karna orders Dussasana to take the serving-woman Draupadi into the inner apartments, and Dussasana drags her before the spectators.

B02C067.summary: Draupadi, dragged before the assembly, appeals to the Kurus, recalling that she was seen by the kings only once, at her swayamvara, and asking whether she is a wife or a servant. She challenges the elders to say whether she was won or not, and accepts their verdict. Bhishma replies that dharma is too subtle for him to settle, that the Kurus are ruined by greed and folly, and that Yudhishthira alone can say whether she was won.

scenes.B02C067S01: Draupadi, dragged in, lays her case before the elders, and Bhishma answers that the question is subtle and must be settled by Yudhishthira.

shots.B02C067S01H01: Draupadi asks Dussasana to wait, saying she has a duty to perform, that she was overpowered by his strength, and that she bows to the elders present.
shots.B02C067S01H02: Draupadi falls to the ground, dragged with greater force, and weeps before the Kuru assembly.
shots.B02C067S01H03: Draupadi recalls her swayamvara, asks whether she is a servant or a wife, condemns the Kurus for allowing the shame, and asks the kings to say whether she is won.
shots.B02C067S01H04: Bhishma says that dharma is subtle, that the Kurus are ruined by greed, and that Yudhishthira must decide whether she was won.

B02C068.summary: Duryodhana taunts Draupadi, telling her that her husbands should answer her question and that Yudhishthira should declare that he is not their lord. Bhima replies that if Yudhishthira regards himself as won, then they are all won, but that he would slay the sons of Dhritarashtra if the eldest commanded it. Bhishma, Drona and Vidura tell him to hold back.

scenes.B02C068S01: Duryodhana taunts Draupadi and the Pandavas, Bhima threatens revenge but holds back, and the elders urge restraint.

shots.B02C068S01H01: Duryodhana, seeing the kings silent, tells Draupadi that her husbands should say whether Yudhishthira is their lord, so that she may be freed from slavery.
shots.B02C068S01H02: The assembly applauds Duryodhana, and Bhima speaks, saying that he and his brothers are bound to Yudhishthira's word and would kill the Kauravas if commanded.
shots.B02C068S01H03: Bhishma, Drona and Vidura tell Bhima to hold back, since with his strength everything is possible.

B02C069.summary: Karna argues that Draupadi, now a slave, should choose another husband, and Duryodhana exposes his thigh to her, which enrages Bhima, who vows to break it. Vidura warns the kings that a disaster is coming, and Arjuna says that Yudhishthira was master until he lost himself. Omens of jackals and braying asses frighten the court, and Dhritarashtra grants Draupadi a boon: the freedom of Yudhishthira and of her son. He offers a second boon, which she accepts for her husbands' freedom, and a third, which she declines.

scenes.B02C069S01: Karna mocks Draupadi as a slave, Duryodhana exposes his thigh, Bhima vows to break it, Vidura warns the kings, and Duryodhana offers to accept Bhima's terms.
scenes.B02C069S02: Arjuna says Yudhishthira was their master only before he lost himself, ill omens sound in the palace, and Dhritarashtra asks Draupadi for a boon.
scenes.B02C069S03: Dhritarashtra grants Draupadi a second boon for the Pandavas' freedom and offers a third, which she declines.

shots.B02C069S01H01: Karna says that the three independent elders, Bhishma, Vidura and Drona, speak against Duryodhana, and that Draupadi, now a slave, should go to the inner apartments and choose another husband.
shots.B02C069S01H02: Bhima, bound by duty to the king, says he cannot be angry at a Suta's son, since they are now in servitude, but he would not bear such words from enemies had the king not staked her.
shots.B02C069S01H03: Duryodhana tells Yudhishthira to answer, then exposes his thigh to Draupadi, and Bhima vows to break it in battle.
shots.B02C069S01H04: Vidura warns the kings that the calamity has come from fate, that the match was improper, and that a stake made by one who has lost himself is like winning a treasure in a dream.
shots.B02C069S01H05: Duryodhana says he will accept whatever Bhima, Arjuna and the twins declare, if they deny that Yudhishthira is their master.
shots.B02C069S02H01: Arjuna says Yudhishthira was their master until he lost himself, and that the Kauravas must judge whose master he can be after that.
shots.B02C069S02H02: A jackal howls in the sacred chamber, asses bray and birds scream, and Bhishma, Drona and Kripa call out a blessing, while Vidura and Gandhari report the omens to Dhritarashtra.
shots.B02C069S02H03: A footnote explains that the blessing used in the text is a word of benediction, like Amen.
shots.B02C069S02H04: Dhritarashtra scolds Duryodhana for insulting the wife of the Kuru princes and offers Draupadi any boon she desires.
shots.B02C069S02H05: Draupadi asks that Yudhishthira be freed from slavery and that her son Prativindhya not be called the son of a slave.
shots.B02C069S03H01: Dhritarashtra agrees and offers her a second boon, saying she deserves more than one.
shots.B02C069S03H02: Draupadi asks that Bhima, Arjuna and the twins, with their chariots and bows, be freed from bondage.
shots.B02C069S03H03: Dhritarashtra grants this and offers a third boon.
shots.B02C069S03H04: Draupadi declines a third boon, citing the rule that a Vaisya may ask one, a Kshatriya woman two and a Brahmana a hundred, and says her husbands will prosper by their own virtue.

B02C070.summary: Karna praises Draupadi as the boat that rescued the Pandavas from the ocean of distress. Bhima laments that the insult to his wife has dimmed the light of his family, and Arjuna answers that superior men do not dwell on the harsh words of inferiors. Bhima, furious, threatens to kill the Kauravas then and there, and Yudhishthira restrains him and goes to speak to Dhritarashtra.

scenes.B02C070S01: Karna praises Draupadi, Bhima laments the insult, Arjuna counsels restraint, and Yudhishthira restrains Bhima and turns to Dhritarashtra.

shots.B02C070S01H01: Karna says Draupadi has saved the Pandavas, becoming a boat for them in a boatless ocean of distress.
shots.B02C070S01H02: Bhima, angered, says that his inner light is dimmed by this insult and asks how a son born of such an insult can be of use.
shots.B02C070S01H03: Arjuna answers that superior men do not remember the harsh words of inferiors, but only their good deeds.
shots.B02C070S01H04: Bhima offers to slay the whole assembly, Arjuna pacifies him, and Yudhishthira embraces Bhima and calms him, then approaches Dhritarashtra with folded hands.

B02C071.summary: Yudhishthira bows to Dhritarashtra and asks for his command. The old king tells him to forget Duryodhana's insults, to return to Indraprastha with his wealth, and to keep to the path of peace and brotherly love. The Pandavas leave with Draupadi for their city.

scenes.B02C071S01: Yudhishthira asks Dhritarashtra for his command, Dhritarashtra counsels peace and forgiveness, and the Pandavas leave for Indraprastha with Draupadi.

shots.B02C071S01H01: Yudhishthira tells Dhritarashtra that he is their master and asks for his command.
shots.B02C071S01H02: Dhritarashtra blesses him, tells him to rule his kingdom with his wealth, and advises him to forgive and not remember Duryodhana's harsh words, reminding him of his mother Gandhari and himself.
shots.B02C071S01H03: Yudhishthira takes his leave with courtesy, and he and his brothers ride with Draupadi toward Indraprastha.

B02C072.summary: Janamejaya asks how the Kauravas reacted to the Pandavas' release. Dussasana complains that Dhritarashtra has thrown away their winnings, and Duryodhana, Karna and Sakuni persuade the king to recall the Pandavas for a second match, staking exile for twelve years and a thirteenth year in disguise. Drona, Somadatta, Kripa, Bhishma and others urge peace, but Dhritarashtra, partial to his sons, ignores them and summons the Pandavas back.

scenes.B02C072S01: Dussasana complains to Duryodhana, Duryodhana, Karna and Sakuni persuade Dhritarashtra to recall the Pandavas for a rematch of exile, and Dhritarashtra agrees.
scenes.B02C072S02: The elders, including Drona, Somadatta, Bhishma and Vikarna, urge peace, but Dhritarashtra ignores them and summons the Pandavas back.

shots.B02C072S01H01: Janamejaya asks how the sons of Dhritarashtra reacted when they learned that the Pandavas had been released with their wealth.
shots.B02C072S01H02: Dussasana tells Duryodhana that their father has returned the Pandavas' wealth, and Duryodhana, Karna and Sakuni go to Dhritarashtra in private.
shots.B02C072S01H03: Duryodhana argues that the Pandavas will attack and proposes a rematch, with the loser to live twelve years in the forest and a thirteenth in disguise.
shots.B02C072S01H04: Dhritarashtra orders that the Pandavas be brought back to play again.
shots.B02C072S01H05: The list of elders begins with Drona, Somadatta, Bahlika and Kripa.
shots.B02C072S02H01: The list continues with names including Ashvatthama, Bhurisravas and Bhishma.
shots.B02C072S02H02: The list names Vikarna, another son of the king, among those counselling against the match.
shots.B02C072S02H03: All of them urge that the play not begin and that there be peace.
shots.B02C072S02H04: Dhritarashtra, partial to his sons, ignores the counsel of his wise friends and relatives.
shots.B02C072S02H05: Dhritarashtra summons the Pandavas back for another match at dice.

B02C073.summary: Gandhari, grieving for her sons, pleads with Dhritarashtra to abandon Duryodhana, recalling Vidura's warning at his birth that he would bring the family's ruin. Dhritarashtra replies that if ruin is fated, it should come, and he orders the Pandavas recalled so that the dice match can resume. The chapter ends with the king surrendering to his son's will.

scenes.B02C073S01: Gandhari pleads with Dhritarashtra to cast off Duryodhana, and Dhritarashtra accepts fate and orders the Pandavas back for another match.

shots.B02C073S01H01: Gandhari reminds Dhritarashtra of Vidura's warning at Duryodhana's birth, begs him not to ruin the race for his sons' sake, and urges him to cast off the wicked youth.
shots.B02C073S01H02: Dhritarashtra says that if the family's ruin is fated, let it come, and that the Pandavas should return so the dice may be cast again.

B02C074.summary: A royal messenger catches up with Yudhishthira, who has gone some distance, and brings Dhritarashtra's summons back to the dice. Yudhishthira accepts, saying fate rules and he cannot refuse the old king, though he knows the match will ruin him. Sakuni sets the new stake as exile: the loser must spend twelve years in the forest in deer-skins and a thirteenth in hiding, after which the kingdom is to be handed back, and Sakuni wins once more.

scenes.B02C074S01: The messenger catches up with Yudhishthira, who turns back to the dice, and Sakuni proposes exile in the forest as the new stake.
scenes.B02C074S02: Yudhishthira accepts the new stake, and Sakuni casts the dice and claims the win.

shots.B02C074S01H01: The royal messenger overtakes Yudhishthira and delivers Dhritarashtra's summons to the dice.
shots.B02C074S01H02: Yudhishthira says fate decides the fruits of action, that he cannot refuse the old king's summons, and that he expects ruin but will go back.
shots.B02C074S01H03: The narrator compares Yudhishthira's fate to Rama's, tempted by a golden deer, and says the brothers return to the hall to play.
shots.B02C074S01H04: Sakuni says the old king has returned their wealth and proposes exile as the stake: twelve years in the forest and a thirteenth year in hiding for the loser.
shots.B02C074S01H05: The assembly cries out that Duryodhana's friends have not warned him of his danger, and that the elders should tell the king plainly.
shots.B02C074S02H01: Yudhishthira, from shame and a sense of duty, sits down to play again, knowing that ruin is near for the Kurus.
shots.B02C074S02H02: Yudhishthira says a king of his order cannot refuse a summons to dice, and agrees to play with Sakuni.
shots.B02C074S02H03: Sakuni lists the old stakes of cattle, horses, gold and slaves, and sets the single stake of exile to the woods for the loser.
shots.B02C074S02H04: Yudhishthira accepts this one stake, and Sakuni casts the dice and says that he has won.

B02C075.summary: The defeated Pandavas put on deer-skins, and Dussasana gloats, mocking them and urging Draupadi to choose another husband. Bhima, furious, vows to tear open Dussasana's breast and drink his blood, and to slay Duryodhana, Karna and Sakuni. Arjuna, Sahadeva and Nakula each swear to avenge Draupadi's insult in the fourteenth year, and the brothers go to take leave of Dhritarashtra.

scenes.B02C075S01: Dussasana gloats over the Pandavas in deer-skins, Bhima answers with threats, and Dussasana mocks him as a cow.
scenes.B02C075S02: Bhima, Arjuna, Sahadeva and Nakula each vow vengeance, to be carried out in the fourteenth year.
scenes.B02C075S03: The brothers approach Dhritarashtra after their vows.

shots.B02C075S01H01: The Pandavas take off their royal robes and put on deer-skins, and Dussasana gloats that the Kauravas now rule, mocking the brothers as grains of sesame without kernel.
shots.B02C075S01H02: Dussasana insults the Pandavas and Draupadi, and Bhima answers that he will pierce his heart in battle and slay the Kauravas and their followers.
shots.B02C075S01H03: Dussasana, shameless, dances around the Kurus and calls out to Bhima mocking him as a cow.
shots.B02C075S01H04: Bhima answers that he will drink Dussasana's blood in battle, and that he will pacify his wrath by slaying the sons of Dhritarashtra.
shots.B02C075S01H05: As the Pandavas leave, Duryodhana mimics Bhima's walk, and Bhima vows to slay Duryodhana and his followers and to drink Dussasana's blood.
shots.B02C075S02H01: Arjuna says that the resolutions of superior men are not spoken but shown, and that the Kauravas will see what happens in the fourteenth year.
shots.B02C075S02H02: Bhima says that the earth will drink the blood of Duryodhana, Karna, Sakuni and Dussasana.
shots.B02C075S02H03: Arjuna vows to slay Karna and his followers and the kings who fight him, and says the vow will stand unless Duryodhana restores their kingdom in the fourteenth year.
shots.B02C075S02H04: Sahadeva vows to slay Sakuni with his followers, calling him the disgrace of the Gandhara kings.
shots.B02C075S02H05: Nakula vows to send the sons of Dhritarashtra to Yama for insulting Draupadi at the match.
shots.B02C075S03H01: The brothers, bound by their vows, approach Dhritarashtra.

B02C076.summary: Yudhishthira bids farewell to the elders, including Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Ashvatthama, Vidura and Dhritarashtra, and the assembly, ashamed, can only pray for his welfare. Vidura asks that Kunti remain in his house, and gives Yudhishthira a long counsel on patience, drawing on the gods, the sages who taught him, and his brothers' strengths. Yudhishthira bows to Bhishma and Drona and goes into exile.

scenes.B02C076S01: Yudhishthira bids farewell to the court, Vidura asks that Kunti be kept in his house, and he gives Yudhishthira a long counsel on endurance and virtue.
scenes.B02C076S02: Yudhishthira bows to Bhishma and Drona and departs.

shots.B02C076S01H01: Yudhishthira bids farewell to Bhishma, Somadatta, Vahlika, Drona, Kripa, Ashvatthama, Vidura, Dhritarashtra, his sons, Yuyutsu and Sanjaya, promising to return.
shots.B02C076S01H02: The courtiers, too ashamed to answer, silently pray for his welfare.
shots.B02C076S01H03: Vidura asks that Kunti, a princess, not go to the forest but stay in his own house.
shots.B02C076S01H04: The Pandavas agree to Vidura's wish, call him their father and respected elder, and ask him to say what else must be done.
shots.B02C076S01H05: Vidura advises Yudhishthira not to grieve at a defeat won by foul means, lists his brothers' strengths and virtues, and blesses him with the powers of the gods and his teachers.
shots.B02C076S02H01: Yudhishthira agrees, bows to Bhishma and Drona, and goes on his way.

B02C077.summary: Draupadi takes leave of Kunti and the household women, and Kunti blesses her and asks her to watch over Sahadeva in the forest. Kunti follows and finds her sons in deer-skins surrounded by rejoicing foes, embraces them, and laments the calamity, calling on Krishna, Pandu and the elders. The Pandavas comfort their mother and leave for the forest, Vidura takes Kunti to his house, and the anxious Dhritarashtra summons Vidura.

scenes.B02C077S01: Draupadi takes leave, Kunti blesses her, and then Kunti, seeing her sons in deer-skins, laments and begs Sahadeva to stay.
scenes.B02C077S02: The Pandavas comfort their mother and go into exile, Vidura takes Kunti to his house, and Dhritarashtra summons Vidura to ask how the Pandavas left.

shots.B02C077S01H01: Draupadi takes leave of Kunti and the household women, who all weep at the loss.
shots.B02C077S01H02: Kunti tells Draupadi not to grieve, praises her chastity and conduct, and asks her to watch over Sahadeva in the woods.
shots.B02C077S01H03: Draupadi leaves weeping in a single blood-stained cloth, Kunti follows, and finds her sons stripped of ornaments, clad in deer-skins and surrounded by rejoicing foes.
shots.B02C077S01H04: Kunti embraces her sons, laments their ruin, calls on Krishna, Pandu, Bhishma and Drona, and begs Sahadeva to stay with her.
shots.B02C077S01H05: A heading marks the start of Section LXXIX.
shots.B02C077S02H01: The Pandavas comfort their mother and set out for the woods, Vidura takes Kunti to his house, and the Kaurava women grieve while Dhritarashtra, anxious for his sons, sends for Vidura.
shots.B02C077S02H02: Vidura comes at once, and Dhritarashtra anxiously asks how the Pandavas left Hastinapura.

B02C078.summary: Dhritarashtra anxiously asks Vidura how each Pandava left the city, and Vidura describes each brother's manner of departure as a sign of his intent, from Bhima flexing his arms to Draupadi weeping with loosened hair. Vidura reports the portents that accompanied them, including earthquake, eclipse and cries of jackals. A celestial sage foretells that the Kauravas will be destroyed in fourteen years, and Drona reassures the Kauravas while warning that Dhrishtadyumna, born to slay him, has joined the Pandavas. Dhritarashtra tells Vidura to bring the Pandavas back with honour.

scenes.B02C078S01: Dhritarashtra asks how each Pandava left, Vidura explains each brother's gesture and the portents, a celestial sage foretells ruin, and Drona warns the Kauravas.
scenes.B02C078S02: Dhritarashtra accepts Drona's counsel and tells Vidura to bring the Pandavas back with honour.

shots.B02C078S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Vidura, in a timid voice, how Yudhishthira, Arjuna, the twins, Dhaumya and Draupadi are faring on their journey.
shots.B02C078S01H02: Vidura describes how each brother departs: Yudhishthira covering his face, Bhima admiring his arms, Arjuna scattering sand, the twins smearing their faces and staining themselves with dust, Draupadi weeping with her hair loose, and Dhaumya chanting Yama's mantras.
shots.B02C078S01H03: Dhritarashtra asks why the Pandavas are leaving Hastinapura in such different guises.
shots.B02C078S01H04: Vidura explains that each gesture signals a resolve, that the citizens lament the Kurus' injustice, and that portents of lightning, an eclipse and jackals and vultures foretell the ruin of the Bharatas.
shots.B02C078S01H05: A celestial sage appears before the assembly and foretells that the Kauravas will be destroyed in fourteen years through Duryodhana's fault, and Drona then warns the Kauravas that Dhrishtadyumna, born to slay him, has sided with the Pandavas.
shots.B02C078S02H01: Dhritarashtra accepts Drona's words and tells Vidura to bring the Pandavas back with weapons, chariots and every honour, or let them go with respect.

B02C079.summary: After the Pandavas go into the forest, Dhritarashtra is restless, and Sanjaya asks why he grieves now that he has the whole earth. Dhritarashtra fears the Pandavas' return, and Sanjaya blames Duryodhana for ignoring the elders and dragging Draupadi into the hall, which he sees as a sign of approaching ruin. Dhritarashtra recounts the omens and admits that he granted Draupadi boons and freed the Pandavas, that Vidura urged peace, and that he refused for love of his son. The chapter closes the Sabha Parva.

scenes.B02C079S01: Sanjaya comforts Dhritarashtra, is answered with fears of the Pandavas' return, blames Duryodhana for the insult to Draupadi, and Dhritarashtra recounts the omens and his failure to take Vidura's counsel.
scenes.B02C079S02: A licence notice that closes the file, not part of the narrative.

shots.B02C079S01H01: After the Pandavas leave for the forest, Dhritarashtra is overcome with anxiety, and Sanjaya asks why he grieves now that he has won the earth and sent the Pandavas into exile.
shots.B02C079S01H02: Dhritarashtra says that he fears the battle with the Pandavas, who will fight in great chariots with allies.
shots.B02C079S01H03: Sanjaya blames Dhritarashtra's mistaken action and Duryodhana's insult to Draupadi, and says that ruin clouds the judgement of those whom the gods mean to destroy.
shots.B02C079S01H04: Dhritarashtra recounts the omens, admits that he freed the Pandavas after Draupadi asked, and recalls that Vidura urged peace with the sons of Pandu, which he refused out of love for his son.
shots.B02C079S01H05: A heading marks the end of the Sabha Parva.
